s1.text:
Design system used across all screens

Paper ground #F4F1EB, ink #1C1B19, one accent (teal #0E6B63). AI content is set as marginalia: gutter glyph, small-caps attribution, reading serif, numbered source footnotes. No stripes, no sparkles. Semantic states differ in lightness, not hue alone. Body 16px IBM Plex Sans; lesson reading in Fraunces serif at 19px / 68ch. Comfortable density for learners, compact for instructors/admins. Every AI output lands as a labeled draft with provenance, diff and undo.

s2.text:
Why these screens differ from Canvas

1. Plan-first generation (Brief → Outline → Draft → Review → Publish) with human checkpoints.
2. Provenance chips + review-coverage meter on every AI-touched block.
3. Policy-bound Socratic tutor: instructor sets hint-only / explain / open per activity; tutor cites course sources.
4. Persona variants generated from one master course.
5. ⌘K palette turns natural language into a previewable change set.
6. QM/WCAG 2.2 linter runs before publish.

Start from a syllabus

The AI is the Design partner, not a generator: it reads the syllabus, cites the page behind every claim, asks before proposing, offers three approaches with trade-offs, previews the change set, and provisions drafts only.
